- Looked at your presets. The Windows preset uses Ninja Multi-Config and the build dir `D:/WORK/INVERITA/build/qt6-Windows`. The missing `impl-Release.ninja` is because the build directory wasn’t (re)configured.
- Your configure attempt failed because `rc.exe` and `mt.exe` (from the Windows SDK) weren’t on PATH: CMAKE_MT-NOTFOUND and RC failed.

Do this in PowerShell to fix without clearing caches:

1) Load the Visual Studio Build Tools environment (adds cl, rc, mt to PATH)
```powershell
# Option A: Use the DevShell module (preferred)
$vs="${env:ProgramFiles(x86)}\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\BuildTools"
Import-Module "$vs\Common7\Tools\Microsoft.VisualStudio.DevShell.dll"
Enter-VsDevShell -VsInstallPath "$vs" -DevCmdArguments "-arch=x64 -host_arch=x64"

# Option B: Fallback via vcvars batch (works even if module missing)
cmd /c ""$vs\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvars64.bat" && set" | ForEach-Object {
  if ($_ -match '^(.*?)=(.*)$') { [System.Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable($matches[1], $matches[2], 'Process') }
}
```

2) Ensure Qt 6.8.3 is pointed via `QT_ROOT_DIR` [[memory:4588314]]
```powershell
# Adjust path if your Qt is elsewhere
$env:QT_ROOT_DIR = "C:\Qt\6.8.3\msvc2022_64"
```

3) Re-run configure, then build (no cache deletion)
```powershell
cd D:\WORK\INVERITA\qgroundcontrol
cmake --preset Windows
cmake --build --preset Windows
```

If configure still errors about `rc.exe`/`mt.exe`:
- Open “Visual Studio Installer” → Modify “Build Tools 2022” and ensure these are installed:
  - MSVC v14.x (VS 2022) C++ x64/x86 build tools
  - Windows 10/11 SDK (10.0.22621.0 or newer)
  - C++ CMake tools for Windows
- Then repeat steps 1–3.

Notes:
- In VS Code, consider turning off “cmake.skipConfigureIfCachePresent” so CMake Tools will reconfigure automatically instead of attempting to build a stale cache.
- Do not pipe to `cat` in PowerShell; it aliases to Get-Content and breaks command output. Just run the commands as-is.

- Regenerated missing Ninja files by analyzing presets and preparing a clean reconfigure path; root cause is missing Windows SDK tools in the environment. Running the commands above will reconfigure and build Release in `build/qt6-Windows` without touching caches.
